chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: "If you perform the ritual bath (ghusl) in Mecca, then sleep before performing the Tawaf, you must repeat your ritual bath."
And when he wishes to enter the Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), let him enter through the Gate of Banu Shaybah.
And let him recite the supplication upon entering; he narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating the ritual bath (ghusl) if one sleeps before performing Tawaf in Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the ritual purity attained through ghusl in Mecca is contingent upon immediate performance of Tawaf; sleeping in between necessitates renewal of the bath, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of ritual state during Hajj rites. Furthermore, the narration prescribes entering the Grand Mosque via the Gate of Banu Shaybah, a specific tradition highlighting the spiritual significance of the entry point in aligning the pilgrim’s physical movement with divine etiquette.
